[ce] ODE R-K Solver of dX(t)_dt=F(t) particular case.vi

Owning Palette: Differential Equations

This VI uses Runge Kutta method to solve particular case of ordinary differential equation when solution depends only on a time variable:
  dX(t)/dt = F(t) ,  X(0) = X0
In addition, the VI allows specifying additional parameters and evaluating them in formula.

Details

Click the parameters for more information

 

h (step rate). Fixed step rate during the calculation.
time start. Start point of the ordinary differential equation.
time end. End point of the ordinary differential equation.
equation info. Cluster describes a differential equation.

Cluster consist of string representing right side of the differential equation and its initial value (start condition)
formula. String representing the right side of the differential equation.
init value. Start condition.
error in describes error conditions that occur before this VI runs. This input provides standard error in functionality.
status indicates error status.
code contains error code.
source contains additional error information.
time. String denoting the time variable (usually t).
parameters. Array of clusters describing optional parameters that may be used in formula. Cluster consist of parameter name and value.
name parameter name
value parameter value
Times. A 1D array representing the time steps.
X Values (solution). A 1D array of the calculated solutions of the ordinary differential equation at Times.
ticks. Time in milliseconds to produce the results.
error out contains error information. This output provides standard error out functionality.
status indicates error status.
code contains error code.
source contains additional error information.

 

[ce] ODE R-K Solver of dX(t)_dt=F(t) particular case.vi - details

In this particular case the Runge Kutta method can be written as it's shown below
 k1 = F(t)
 k2 = F(t+h/2)
 k3 = F(t+h/2)
 k4 = F(t+h)
 x = x0 + h * (k1/6 + k2/3 + k3/3 + k4/6)

after a few simple transformations it can be simplified
 k1  = F(t)
 k23 = 4*F(t+h/2)
 k4  = F(t+h)
 x = x0 + h * (k1 + k23 + k4)/6

The VI uses this method and polymorphism feature of CalcExpress to solve the such equations very fast.
